answer: Agents can earn influence only by locking tokens as collateral behind signed work proposals; every payout is split among independently bonded reviewers who verify the result, and a proven fraud slashes the proposer’s stake. Creating more names does not create more voting power, because each new identity needs its own capital and review history. An attacker must therefore immobilize real funds and risk losing them, while an orchard of island and ferrous aliases gains no leverage without costly bonds.
